newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call buyers flock to K-Mart.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call buyers flock to K-Mart.

text.p: A solid second quarter earnings report and an afternoon upgrade boosted shares of K Mart Corp and continued to draw call buyers to the options, traders said Thursday.
"It seems like we've got nothing but call buyers at this point," a market maker in the options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) said.
He added that the trading was under fast market conditions, meaning that because of market conditions, prices indicated on brokers screens may not be current.
In afternoon trading, the retailer's stock was ahead 1-1/8 at 12-7/8 on hevay volume of more than 8.6 million shares.
Among the K Mart calls, the September 12-1/2s traded about 5,585 contracts. It was up 1/2 at 15/16 and had open interest of 26,664.
The September 15 calls traded 2,360 contracts and gained 3/16 to 5/16. It had open interest of 23,592 contracts.
Todd Salamone, an analyst at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said the heavy call open interest at the 12-1/2 strike could have potentially served as call related resistance.
"Certainly the fact that it is above there" is a positive development, he said. "It does have fundamentals in terms of earnings momentum driving it higher."
He added that some of the stock's gains could have been fueled by market makers doing some delta hedging as the stock moved through the 12-1/2 strike price.
"As the stock moves in the money, they have to become more hedged so they don't get burned," he said. "That could be what's going on there."
Delta hedging is done by market makers to keep their positions neutral.
Delta is the amount by which an option price will change for a one-point change in the underlying.
Salamone added that a couple of closes above the 12-1/2 level would be needed to confirm the stock's breakout above that level.
Among other K Mart calls, the August 12-1/2 traded 4,875 contracts, the December 12-1/2 traded 750 and the January 12-1/2 traded about 815.
"There are a lot of 12s trading," the market maker said, adding that the stock shot up to its highs after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to strong buy from outperform.
Early Thursday, K Mart reported second quarter earnings from continuing operations of $0.06 a share, up from $0.05 a share in the 1996 second quarter.
The earnings beat Wall Street's mean estimate of $0.04 as well as the company's own forecast made in early July that its second quarter profits would fall short of the 1996 second quarter result.
"It was an impressive earnings report," Salamone said. "They came out two pennies above the mean estimate but that was 50 percent above the estimate," he said.
